action: Test the stable repository-id metadata surface as a zero-cost Chat-visible discriminator for repository-object substitution, while preserving same-repository ref rewind as unresolved.

connected_surface.selector_semantics: The connected GitHub get-repository capability accepts a numeric repository_id described as the stable repository id from a GitHub repository object.

public_sources.title: Using global node IDs - GitHub Docs
public_sources.relevance: GitHub documents node_id as an object identifier usable for direct node lookup and recommends persisting it to reference the same object across API versions.

public_sources.title: Restoring a deleted repository - GitHub Docs
public_sources.relevance: GitHub distinguishes restoration of a deleted repository from creating a replacement repository; restoration can be available for up to 90 days, so restore must not be conflated with delete-then-new-create in an incarnation test.

result.clone_or_copy_to_distinct_github_reposit: A distinct GitHub repository object has a distinct object identity; a pinned repository-id/node-id guard can therefore reject substitution by a copy hosted as a different repository object, even if owner/name/content resemble the original. This was established from repository-object identity semantics and connected metadata, not by creating a live copy.
result.ordinary_branch_update: No conflict with the repository-object guard: branch/ref movement occurs within the same repository object and therefore does not require changing the pinned repository identity.
result.same_repository_force_ref_rewind: NOT DETECTED. Rewinding a ref inside the same repository leaves repository-object identity unchanged, so r202's same-repository ABA remains unresolved.
result.delete_then_new_repository_same_path: LIKELY DETECTED by a pinned object identity because the replacement is a new repository object; however this run did not perform destructive mutation and the cited public docs do not provide a direct no-ID-reuse theorem for numeric REST ids. Treat this as source-supported architecture inference, not an empirical guarantee.
result.restore_deleted_repository: OUTSIDE THE NEW-INCARNATION CLAIM. GitHub exposes restoration as recovery of a deleted repository; identity preservation across restore was not verified here and must not be used as positive anti-ABA evidence.
result.bottom_line: Repository incarnation identity closes clone/copy/new-object substitution cheaply, but cannot by itself supply the non-rewindable monotonic fact required for same-repository force-ref ABA. It should be composed with, not substituted for, a monotonic/incarnation counter if that later becomes Chat-visible.
